reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that valid inference depends on classification validity—when entities are properly grouped, their behaviors can inform each other. However, similarity alone is insufficient; it must rest on shared properties capable of supporting logical inference. This leads to a duality: while classification enables prediction, its failure results in unreliable extrapolation. Knowledge limitation further constrains this process, as human cognition operates within finite informational bounds. Thus, risk emerges from both flawed classification and incomplete knowledge. Profit arises when one exploits these limitations strategically, either through superior classification or by operating within acceptable error margins. The epistemic failure modes include overgeneralization due to spurious similarity and overconfidence in uncertain inferences.
